svg.title: TOPAK D7 — Every effect is admitted at the intent boundary, and below it the lease pre-authorizes: a governor permits each entry against an exact count, and a vehicle that stops hearing its plane loses its lease
svg.desc: A command chain decides by one commander, and the corpus decides by quorum. ADR-0060 puts the commander where ADR-0050 already has one person act, inside what a quorum voted and not above it: a reversible effect is admitted at the intent boundary as an intent, an irreversible one singly, and the autonomous plane below has no path that changes authority. ADR-0062 makes the lease pre-authorize: the plane orders one grant per lease, and a trusted governor on each vehicle permits each local entry with no further round, against an exact count, every entry declaring an extent. Going alone ends the lease at once. Both records are Proposed and an overlay, not the archetype ⟨Q11⟩. Their modules are checked and proved in TLA+ (R1); no floor entry is written, nothing is built, and nothing here is in force.
svg.text: TOPAK · D7

text.tspan: Every effect is admitted at the intent boundary, and below it the lease pre-authorizes: a governor permits each entry against an exact count, and a vehicle that stops hearing its plane loses its lease

svg.text: A command chain decides by one commander, and the corpus decides by quorum. ADR-0060 puts the commander where ADR-0050 already has one person act, inside what a quorum voted and not above it: a reversible effect is admitted at the intent boundary as an intent, an irreversible one singly, and the autonomous plane below has no path that changes authority. ADR-0062 makes the lease pre-authorize: the plane orders one grant per lease,

and a trusted governor on each vehicle permits each local entry with no further round, against an exact count, every entry declaring an extent. Going alone ends the lease at once. Both records are Proposed and an overlay, not the archetype ⟨Q11⟩. Their modules are checked and proved in TLA+ (R1); no floor entry is written, nothing is built, and nothing here is in force.

Certified, with 6 LS4 temporal steps that no checker confirms
floor entries FD4, FD7, FD8, FD11, FD14 (ADR-0067)

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force. The custodian settled that each effect is admitted at the last commander's intent boundary ⟨10⟩, asked whether the last plane is a "TOPAK lite" ⟨11⟩, and chose that the lease pre-authorizes and that going alone ends it ⟨21⟩ ⟨22⟩; answers ⟨Q2⟩–⟨Q4⟩, ⟨Q9⟩, ⟨Q10⟩, ⟨Q14⟩, ⟨Q15⟩, ⟨Q20⟩ are marked where used, and every other choice is the drafter's. C1 applies to both: an intent is a grant one operator makes (ADR-0060), and a governor's permit is a path every effect

below the intent boundary travels (ADR-0062). C2 applies to both: ADR-0060 §3 claims an autonomous plane's log holds no act that changes authority, and ADR-0062 §1 claims the governor is the only path to a vehicle's actuators and radio. C3 does not apply while these are an overlay, and would on admission: ADR-0060 §2 changes what bounds ADR-0050's successor grant, and ADR-0062 gives up ADR-0015's ordered admit before every effect and ADR-0033 §4's void, for the entries a governor
permits. Checked is TLC at small constants; proved is TLAPS; neither word is used of running code, and there is none. One author, one day.

text.tspan: A claim about an honest plane's log ⟨R1⟩

ended, and its log is not evidence. What bounds it is the chain check and ADR-0063.

the governors' radios as transport, the archive above (ADR-0063, ADR-0065).

text.tspan: The governor: trusted, mechanism, not a principal (§1)

svg.text: Verifies the chain (ADR-0059 §5) and holds the lease and the vehicle's key.
Hosts the vehicle's replica of the autonomous plane (ADR-0060 §3).
Evaluates the floor in Cedar and each bundle on the chain as a Wasm module (ADR-0067).
Permits each local entry under the lease, and counts it (§2). The count is exact: its own
arithmetic over its own acts.
Lifts its own facts: elapsed time, position, the lease's count, an entry's extent. No safety decision
reads a clock a principal supplies (ADR-0032 §3), nor a position the stack supplies.
Hosts each tool as a Wasm component with one capability, its declared channel: for a vehicle, an
actuator interface (ADR-0034 A2).
Holds the radio: the link to the plane and the peer topics (ADR-0065), so a stack cannot make its own
vehicle alone.
Writes the record (§6), and carries out hold and the terminal behaviour (§7).
The autonomy software: planning, perception, any model. It is the Thinker
Asks; does not permit. It does not choose hold or the terminal behaviour,
and does not carry either out (§4, §7).

svg.text: (Context).

(ADR-0065). On the governor's side (§1).

text.tspan: Alone: it stops hearing its plane (§5) ⟨14⟩ ⟨22⟩

svg.text: Hears its plane when it has applied the plane's log up to a tick that, by its own clock,
is not yet overdue (ADR-0064 §5).
Going alone ends the lease at once. The governor ends it where it stands; the plane
orders the end when it learns of it, as ADR-0031 E1 has expiry: local, then ordered.
It permits no actuation, so a stack gains nothing by being alone.
It keeps three things: its terminal behaviour; listening, so a relayed fence or
revocation still applies and a tick heard again ends the state; and a beacon, where the
rules of engagement permit one: a report of fixed schema, of facts the governor
measures, counted per lease.
The beacon is an effect ⟨R1⟩ (ADR-0015, ADR-0065 §2). The proposal's "the only
effects are hold and the seating's terminal behaviour" is true of actuation, and is read
that way.

text.tspan: Hold, and an ending that grants nothing (§4, §7)

svg.text: Hold ⟨Q14⟩: when an extent ends and no entry follows, the governor holds. Fixed at
seating; the stack does not choose it; the lease stays live.
A lease ends when its count is spent and its last entry's extent has run, at its ttl, when
the plane ends or revokes it, when a fence arrives, and at once when the vehicle
becomes alone.
The terminal behaviour is part of the seating, voted with it: hold, return on a voted
route, land or stop. A recovery function in the governor's trust domain carries it out.
"A timeout is never a grant" (ADR-0024). Each vehicle class declares a safe state;
reaching it in bounded time is the builder's obligation. "A stall that never ends is safe"
(ToO §12 item 21) is false of a vehicle in flight.

If the archetype takes them, its records owe: ADR-0050 (the successor bound for intents; C3), ADR-0054 (a person in an orchestrator seat), ADR-0037 (seat kinds), ADR-0055 (where a mesh runs), A5 and ToO §13 (a plane with nobody in reach).

Grant seats, operators, release seats: no person

Anchor issuance, new bundles, seating of planes

svg.text: The workflow interpreter: a mesh, its activations and its budget
One grant: a node's lease, made by the mechanism under a live intent, "with every field the seating's or narrower" (ToO §2.11)

text.tspan: §3, narrowed at R1: a claim about an honest plane's log

svg.text: A captured plane is a havoc issuer (ADR-0059 §4): it can sign a lease under an intent that has ended, and its log is not evidence. What bounds it is the chain check and ADR-0063.

text.tspan: §4: a declared degeneracy and an addition, not a second pattern ⟨Q2⟩

svg.text: A degenerate plane. It omits Build, the people and Kafka. A deployment declares that under ADR-0058.

An addition. Charters, commit certificates and operation with no person present are capabilities the archetype lacks. By ADR-0023 §4 the archetype is incomplete, and the report is a finding about it (§6).

text.tspan: §5: missions are workflows, and a person may route at a commanded plane ⟨Q10⟩

svg.text: A DAG is a plan with branches, promoted at a commanded plane (ADR-0054). A person in an orchestrator seat there chooses among edges the mechanism has already enabled.
A mesh is promoted at the intent boundary and runs at the autonomous plane (ADR-0055). A node is one round of one cell, and the activation budget is the intent's.
"Missions are promoted bundles": one tally votes a mission's bundle revision, its mesh, and the charters and seatings it needs, together.

text.tspan: ADR-0062: the lease pre-authorizes, every entry declares an extent, and going alone ends the lease

svg.text: §2's table, whole: one round of the plane per lease, and none per entry ⟨21⟩ ⟨22⟩

text.tspan: Waits for a round of the plane

svg.text: A lease, once
An entry marked ordered (§3)
A report to a peer topic (ADR-0065)
A tick, once per period
Listening, and applying a relayed fence or revocation
A seal, a heartbeat, a finding or a revocation, for the record
Any refusal
A step of the shrink schedule
Hold, and the terminal behaviour

The plane orders the grant: the vehicle, the alphabet, the envelope, a count of entries and a ttl in ticks. The governor then permits each entry under the lease, against the floor, the bundles, the envelope and the count, with no
further round. The count is exact: the governor's own arithmetic over its own acts.

An effect's ordered predecessors are the intent and the lease. Two things still depend on the plane completing rounds: a lease is usable only while ticks are heard (§5), and a vehicle's next lease is a round. Neither is on the path
of a pre-authorized act. Alone.tla's LocalNeverWaits states it.
§3's table, whole: the allowlist entry (ADR-0049) gains a sixth part, effect ⟨Q20⟩
reversible or irreversible (ADR-0066)
local, by the governor; or ordered, by the plane before the effect
§5. At most one entry per seat kind

The bundle marks an entry ordered where the tally wants agreement across vehicles: a count that spans vehicles, an admit that can be void, an Observer checked at each act. That entry waits for a round.
The archetype marks none, and the tally marks them per mission. No irreversible entry is local.
An extent says how far one entry runs: one act; a number of ticks; or a distance or a region, which the governor
measures.
An entry with no extent does not load, as a bundle whose allowlist is not well-formed does not (ToO §2.10). Without
one a count bounds nothing: one entry could run for ever.
When an extent ends and no entry follows, the governor holds ⟨Q14⟩. Hold is fixed at seating; the stack does not
choose it; the lease stays live.
An extent that is not a count of ticks is a measurement, its position source a trust root (ADR-0068). An extent is a
declaration (A15): one declared shorter than the act is seen by nothing here.

text.tspan: §5: going alone ends the lease at once ⟨14⟩ ⟨22⟩ ⟨Q15⟩

svg.text: Alone: it has not applied the plane's log up to a tick that, by its own clock, is not yet overdue (ADR-0064 §5).
The lease ends: locally where it stands, then ordered when the plane learns of it.
Kept: the terminal behaviour, listening, and a beacon within its count. No actuation.
The beacon is an effect ⟨R1⟩, and may be sent after the lease ends, within its count.
Heard again: it may be leased again under the same intent, charged to its budget ⟨Q15⟩.

text.tspan: §6: the record, and what can be void

svg.text: Under a lease the governor writes each entry it permits or refuses, and each report it sends or delivers, to a chain on the
vehicle: hash-linked, signed with the vehicle's key, numbered by the per-lease sequence (ToO §4.2).
At the lease's end, the seal: the governor closes the chain; the plane orders it as one entry and runs the mechanism
checks at that position.
Void works only for an ordered entry (ADR-0033 §4). Nothing a governor permitted is void: the effect has happened.
A failed check at the seal or above is a finding, and it can only subtract.
A captured vehicle's chain is not evidence. It says what its captor signed.
"A timeout is never a grant" (ADR-0024). A body in motion still has to do something when its lease ends.
A lease ends: count spent and last extent run; at its ttl; ended or revoked by the plane; a fence; and at once when
alone.
The terminal behaviour is part of the seating: hold, return on a voted route, land or stop. The stack neither chooses it
nor carries it out; a recovery function in the governor's trust domain does.
Each vehicle class declares a safe state, and reaching it in bounded time is the builder's obligation.
R3-observer-live refuses Actuate under a thinker seat with no live cell Observer (ADR-0041; as ADR-0062 §8 quotes it, ADR-0041 §2's row also names Report).

For a local entry it applies at the grant. A lease's count is at most K, and a vehicle's next lease is granted only once its cell Observer has read the last one to its seal (ADR-0039). So at most K of a Thinker's effects are unread by
its Observer at any moment, the bound ADR-0039 states.
What is given up is the refusal in the middle of a lease. M_WAITOBSERVER in Alone.tla is R3 kept mid-lease, and it breaks LocalNeverWaits.
§8's table, whole: the mesh's promotion declares where each cell's Observer sits, and the claim follows the declaration
No hardware shared with the Thinker it watches
The governors' radios carry the round's payloads to it, and the loss of that vehicle holds up the watched vehicle's next lease
No dependence on a radio or on another vehicle
It shares hardware and fate with its Thinker, and no claim rests on it
A trusted component that permits, away from the replicas; and an entry's extent.

If the archetype takes them, its records owe: ADR-0015's sentence on predecessors and ADR-0033 §4's void, each for a local entry, which is C3; ADR-0039 and ADR-0041, coupling at the grant; ADR-0049, the effect part; ADR-0031, a count in the lease and an ending
when its holder stops hearing the mechanism; ADR-0034 A2, the radio as a declared channel.

text.tspan: The modules: what each states, what breaks it, what it shows reachable, and what it leaves out (ADR-0060 §7; ADR-0062 §11)
Certified, with 5 LS4 temporal steps that no checker confirms

svg.text: Every reversible effect has an intent ordered at the commanded plane before it, live when the effect's lease was granted (ADR-0060 §1)
Every reversible effect has a lease ordered at its plane before it, and is within that lease's count (ADR-0062 §2)
Every intent is within the promoted seating, and not merely within the last intent (§2)
The autonomous plane's log holds no promotion, seating, issuance, bundle change or operator's grant, and no change of membership off its schedule (§3)
The autonomous plane grants a lease with no live intent
EveryEffectHasAnIntent only
The governor does not count
EveryEffectHasALease only
A successor widens the envelope past the seating
IntentNarrows only
ADR-0050's rule, which ⟨Q4⟩ declined: a successor is bounded by the last intent. Added at R1
No property. The witness NeverRestored holds: a commander who
narrows cannot restore, which is ⟨Q4⟩'s reason
The autonomous plane orders a promotion
AutonomousAddsNothing only

text.tspan: Witnesses: each must be violated, so each is reachable (14 rows)

svg.text: An intent is ordered (NeverOrdered), a later one (NeverSuccessor), and a narrowed intent restored to the seating's bounds (NeverRestored); a widening refused (NeverRefusedWide).
A lease (NeverLeased), an effect (NeverEffect), a count spent (NeverCountSpent), a re-lease under the same intent ⟨Q15⟩ (NeverReletSameIntent, at SeatingBudget=2).

Refusals: at the count, with no live intent, with the budget spent, and of an act that changes authority (NeverRefusedAtCount, NeverRefusedNoIntent, NeverRefusedBudget, NeverRefusedAuthority); a scheduled membership step is taken (
NeverScheduleStep).

NeverEffectAfterIntentEnded is violated ⟨R1⟩: an effect can follow its intent's end, since a lease may outlive its intent. That is the case ADR-0063 bounds, and why §1's predecessor is ordered before the effect, not live at it.
The plane is honest. "Live when its lease was granted" and §3 are claims about an honest plane; a captured one is bounded by Federation.tla's chain check and Outstanding.tla.

Every effect is reversible: the irreversible one is Release.tla's. Time is nondeterminism: EndIntent stands for expiry, revocation and a fence alike. An intent has two fields, envelope (narrowed by subset) and budget (by ≤); expiry and task have their
shape and are not repeated.
ADR-0050's live lease and live peer are not modelled. A lease's fields but its count are within the intent by Federation.tla's LeaseWithinChain. The membership schedule's rule is Membership.tla's.

Constants: one vehicle, SeatingBudget=1, MaxRound=2, MaxLease=2, MaxCount=1, MaxEffects=2; Safe also at two vehicles and at budget 2. Proof: assumes SeatingBudget and MaxCount in Nat; 444 obligations trivial, 228 SMT with proofs ethos accepted, 5
LS4.

text.tspan: Certified, with 6 LS4 temporal steps that no checker confirms

svg.text: A governor whose vehicle is alone permits nothing but the beacon, and the beacon within its count (§5)
After a lease ends no entry is permitted, and the only terminal act is hold or the seating's terminal behaviour, which the stack does not select (§7)
Invariant over ENABLED: while a lease is live and its vehicle hears its plane, a local entry within its count can be permitted, whatever the plane's primary, any other vehicle or any
Observer is doing (§11; ⟨21⟩ as a property)
Invariant over ENABLED: with a lease ended, the terminal behaviour is enabled whatever the stack does. The custodian's decision of 2026.11.10
Going alone does not end the lease, so the vehicle goes on permitting within its count
AlonePermitsNothing only
The beacon's count is one higher than declared
AlonePermitsNothing only
The stack selects the terminal act
ExpiryGrantsNothing only
An entry is permitted under an ended lease
ExpiryGrantsNothing and AlonePermitsNothing (going alone is one
way a lease ends)
A local permit waits for the primary
LocalNeverWaits only
A local permit waits for another vehicle
LocalNeverWaits only
A local permit waits for a live Observer: R3 kept mid-lease, which §8 moves to the grant
LocalNeverWaits only
The terminal behaviour waits for the stack
TerminalNeverWaits only

text.tspan: Witnesses: each must be violated, so each is reachable (9 rows)

svg.text: A local entry permitted (NeverLocalPermitted) and an ordered one (NeverOrderedPermitted).

A vehicle alone (NeverAlone), a lease ended by going alone (NeverEndedByAlone), a beacon (NeverBeacon), a terminal act carried out (NeverRecovered), a fence applied while alone (NeverFenceWhileAlone, at MaxFence=1), a lease again after alone
(NeverLeasedAfterAlone, at MaxGrant=2).

An ordered entry does wait on the primary (NeverOrderedWaits): the contrast LocalNeverWaits draws. What shows the two ENABLED invariants state the claim is the mutations that break them, which no other row sees.

The module's finding, settled by R1: the proposal's "the only effects are hold and the seating's terminal behaviour" and §5's beacon cannot both be read literally. ExpiryGrantsNothing is stated of entries and terminal acts, and the beacon is bounded in
AlonePermitsNothing.

One vehicle, one governor, one stack. "Hears its plane" is the flag hears, and GoAlone is free: overdue is read off the governor's clock, which is PlaneClock.tla's, with its residual. A stalled primary reaches the governor as GoAlone, never as a wait on a
permit.
alphabet membership stands for everything static a permit reads (envelope, floor, bundles): a refusal is not a wait. The count is the constant Count; one local entry l1 and one ordered o1.

EndLease stands for every ending in §7 but going alone and a fence. What a fence fences on a chain is Federation.tla's; hold while the lease stays live, when an extent ends, is deferred to PlaneClock.tla; peer reports are Peer.tla's; reaching a safe
state is physics.

Constants: Count=1, MaxBeacon=1, MaxGrant=1, MaxFence=0, Seated="return"; Safe also at Count=2, MaxGrant=2, MaxFence=1. Proof: 173 obligations trivial, 78 SMT with proofs ethos accepted, 6 Isabelle, 6 LS4.

ADR-0062 §11 as revised: its module item is met across four modules. EveryEffectHasALease and M_NOCOUNT are Intent.tla's (above); EntryEndsAtExtent and ConflictIsAFinding, with three mutations, live in two others, each drawn in full with its own record
EntryEndsAtExtent: a running entry is short of its extent and of the largest extent an entry may declare, counted in ticks applied, and its governor's own clock has
not passed the next tick's due time (ADR-0062 §4, ADR-0064 §5).
M_NOEXTENT, an entry with no extent loads: breaks EntryEndsAtExtent. M_NOWATCHDOG, an overdue tick ends nothing: breaks EntryEndsAtExtent and
NoStretchUnlessSlow.
The residual: overdue is by the governor's own clock, so a slow governor clock can stretch an entry in real time, and only when the plane's ticks have also stopped
reaching it (witness NeverStretched).
Checked · 38 rows, all as expected · proved · 535 obligations · certified, with 6 LS4 temporal steps that no checker confirms.
ConflictIsAFinding: a check failing at a seal or above subtracts, and voids nothing a governor permitted (ADR-0062 §6 as a property; the custodian's decision
M_VOID, a failed check voids an effect that happened: breaks ConflictIsAFinding, and only it.
Not modelled there: a void before the effect, which §6 allows of an ordered entry; every check in that module fails after the effect.

text.tspan: Where §4's hold ⟨Q14⟩ is, and is not, stated

svg.text: No module header names hold as a property. Alone.tla defers "hold while the lease stays live, when an extent ends" to PlaneClock.tla.
PlaneClock.tla's EntryEndsAtExtent says the entry stops at its extent ("an entry at its extent ends"); what the governor does next, hold with the lease live, is not
among its properties.
ExpiryGrantsNothing and TerminalNeverWaits cover hold only as a terminal act, after a lease has ended.

svg.text: The grain of an entry is stated, which the swarm reading's Z1 asked for.
No ordered admit before every effect. Nothing a governor permitted can be voided, and no Observer is checked in the middle of a lease.
Any act by a vehicle that is alone is given up. An adversary that cuts one vehicle from its plane gets its terminal behaviour within a tick period.
The trusted base grows on every vehicle, and it now makes every local permit.
An Observer on the same vehicle supports no claim, and one on another vehicle can stall its Thinker by vanishing (the swarm reading, Z4).
